messages:
amanda: FYI multiple customers reporting 503/500 from hosted embeddings between 10:12-10:18 UTC. Gateway shows upstream infer-worker exits. attaching initial log excerpt.

oncall-bot: ALERT: hosted-embeds: instance=runner-42 exited (code=137) at 2026-03-17T10:14:05Z — auto-retries: 3 — impact: high :rotating_light:

amanda: snippet from /var/log/infer/runner-42.log:
```
[10:14:05] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY)
[10:14:05] infer: uncaught exception: std::bad_alloc
[10:14:05] infer: exiting with signal 9
```

diego: oncall checking host GPU metrics now — memory usage spiked to 98% during an embed-batch spike. p95 allocs up ~3x for embeddings QPS.

raj: probable GPU OOM on coldstart with large batch+kv-prefetch; embedding jobs are allocating full KV cache for long contexts even though not needed. can we repro?

jess: CS: customers impacted: MapleHealth (prod), LarkAnalytics (staging). MapleHealth saw a ~15m window of 503s and opened a support ticket. They say their embed payloads are large (avg 25k tokens).

kevin: quick mitigation: add a routing rule to send MapleHealth to a dedicated lower-batch pool (cpu-fallback or smaller model) and throttle their max batch_size to 8. I can push a routing policy change now if oncall approves.

cs-rep: Please do — MapleHealth is asking for an ETA. They can't tolerate more >1% 5xx.

amanda: please push routing change, kevin. Also disable aggressive kv-prefetch for embeddings globally until we confirm.

kevin: pushing policy now: `rbac:routes -> set MapleHealth -> pool:dedicated-small, max_batch:8`

oncall-bot: ACTION: routing policy updated by kevin at 10:21 UTC — affected requests now routed to dedicated-small.

diego: collecting core dump, nvml logs, and dmesg from runner-42. saving to /tmp/triage/7975312468/. grabbing stack traces.

raj: for repro: send a 25k-token embeddings payload with concurrency ~50 to hosted-embeds endpoint. that'll hit the same allocation path. IIRC we saw it on heavy embed bursts during cold KV alloc.

amanda: can we add a short-term guard in runtime to cap per-request GPU allocation for embeddings or fall back to CPU for single huge requests?

kevin: adding a soft cap (reject >20k token single-request) would be quickest. that'll avoid eating full KV on one request. pushing a hotfix to the routing/runtime gate in the next 30m.

jess: told MapleHealth we routed them to dedicated-small and applied limits; asked if they can lower per-request size as well. they're ok for now but want root cause and timeline.

diego: dumps uploaded: `/tmp/triage/7975312468/{core, nvml.log, dmesg, runtime-stderr}`. quick trace shows alloc path in kv_cache::reserve_for_context -> cudaMalloc -> OOM. not a segfault, OOM then killed (OOM -> SIGKILL).

raj: follow-ups: 1) reproduce on staging with same payload and concurrency, 2) add smaller KV allocation heuristics for embeddings, 3) add better circuit-breaker for single huge requests.

amanda: prioritizing runbook steps: repro test (eng-ml), apply soft caps (eng-runtime), notify CS and customers (jess). I'll own coordinating.

kevin: rolled a runtime gate to reject single-requests >20k tokens at 10:46 UTC. will monitor 10m.

oncall-bot: NOTE: runtime-gate deploy by kevin succeeded at 10:46:12 UTC.

jess: MapleHealth updated: they acknowledged workaround and will adjust payloads. requesting postmortem once root cause fixed.

amanda: next: schedule a follow-up postmortem + CSD (customer summary doc) if we confirm a code fix. tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml to sync tomorrow. 

kevin: for triage notes — not a kernel crash or segfault, it's a GPU OOM during KV cold allocation on embed-heavy coldstart. mitigations applied (routing + soft cap).

amanda: thanks all. closing immediate escalation; will re-open if we see another upstream exit or residual 5xxs. :thumbsup:
